metadata.title: Bevacizumab 5mg/kg and Modified FOLFOX-6 Therapy -14 day
metadata.indication: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum.

validation.audit_fixes_scope: v0.83.2 live-audit findings; see docs/RELEASE_v0833_CLINICAL_FIXES.md. Independent clinical/pharmacy validation pending.

metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

encoding_maturity.label: Encoded protocol · full source coverage review pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: The protocol has executable SACTCheck content but has not yet completed the v0.68.0 full source fidelity review. Use the current NCCP source as authoritative.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.
metadata.schedule_summary: Day 1: bevacizumab, oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. A cycle lasts 14 days; your team confirms the next treatment.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: JSON assessment encoding for NCCP 00446 Version 7b. Audit corrections reconciled to this regimen's current source on 16 October 2026. Confirm the official PDF and use independent clinical judgement. Clinical and oncology-pharmacy validation remain pending.

indications.description: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum.

output_templates.contraindicated: The entered data trigger a protocol exclusion or contraindication pathway.
output_templates.discontinue: The entered data trigger protocol discontinuation.
output_templates.withhold: Hold treatment and follow the protocol reassessment pathway.
output_templates.consultant_review: Consultant review is required before treatment proceeds.

rule_engine.conflict_policy: Use the most restrictive overall action; combine component changes using the greatest reduction per component rather than summing reductions.
rule_engine.missing_data_policy: Evaluate only supplied values; do not infer missing values. Eligibility/context fields remain optional unless a specific rule requires them.

rules.explanation: Known hypersensitivity to oxaliplatin, 5-fluorouracil or an excipient is an exclusion.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding are protocol exclusions.
Peripheral neuropathy with functional impairment before cycle 1 is an exclusion.
Known complete DPD deficiency is an exclusion to fluoropyrimidine treatment in this regimen.

action.recommendation: Consider a reduced starting 5-FU dose with careful subsequent titration.

rules.explanation: Partial DPD deficiency requires individualised Consultant-directed fluoropyrimidine dosing.

action.recommendation: Confirm DPD status before treatment.

rules.explanation: DPD status has not been confirmed.

action.recommendation: ANC remains below 1.5 ×10⁹/L or platelets below 75 ×10⁹/L after four delayed weeks. Bevacizumab may be delayed independently; review its own criteria and the timing of subsequent treatment (page 3).

rules.explanation: ANC remains below 1.5 ×10⁹/L or platelets below 75 ×10⁹/L after four delayed weeks.

action.recommendation: The day-1 ANC or platelet threshold is not met; hold mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy and repeat FBC weekly. Confirm delay duration and the persistent-toxicity stopping pathway before rescheduling. Bevacizumab may be delayed independently; review its own criteria and the timing of subsequent treatment (page 3).

rules.explanation: The day-1 ANC or platelet threshold is not met; hold mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy and repeat FBC weekly.
After count recovery, an ANC nadir of 0.5–0.99 ×10⁹/L requires a one-level oxaliplatin reduction.
After count recovery, an ANC nadir below 0.5 ×10⁹/L requires oxaliplatin reduction, omission of bolus 5-FU/folinic acid and one-level infusional 5-FU reduction.
After platelet recovery, a nadir of 10–49.9 ×10⁹/L requires a one-level oxaliplatin reduction.
After platelet recovery, a nadir below 10 ×10⁹/L requires a two-level oxaliplatin reduction.
Grade 2 neuropathy at the start of a cycle requires a one-level oxaliplatin reduction.
The first or second occurrence of grade 3 neuropathy requires a one-level oxaliplatin reduction.
Persistent grade 3 neuropathy requires discontinuation of oxaliplatin.
Grade 4 neuropathy requires discontinuation of oxaliplatin.

action.recommendation: Increase the oxaliplatin infusion time from 2 to 6 hours.

rules.explanation: Laryngo-pharyngeal dysaesthesia requires prolongation of oxaliplatin infusion to 6 hours.

action.until: interstitial lung disease or pulmonary fibrosis is excluded

rules.explanation: Withhold oxaliplatin until interstitial lung disease or pulmonary fibrosis is excluded.

action.recommendation: Diarrhoea remains grade 2 or greater after four weeks; discontinue mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy. Bevacizumab may be delayed independently; review its own criteria and the timing of subsequent treatment (page 3).

rules.explanation: Diarrhoea remains grade 2 or greater after four weeks; discontinue mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy.

action.recommendation: Grade 2 or greater diarrhoea on day 1 requires mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy to be held and reviewed weekly. Confirm delay duration and the persistent-toxicity stopping pathway before rescheduling. Bevacizumab may be delayed independently; review its own criteria and the timing of subsequent treatment (page 3).

rules.explanation: Grade 2 or greater diarrhoea on day 1 requires mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy to be held and reviewed weekly.
After recovery from grade 3 diarrhoea, reduce bolus and infusional 5-FU by one dose level.
After recovery from grade 4 diarrhoea, reduce oxaliplatin, bolus 5-FU and infusional 5-FU by one dose level.

action.recommendation: Delay mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy until stomatitis is grade 1 or less. This source does not specify a two-week stopping rule or a grade-specific stomatitis dose reduction. Assess bevacizumab independently.

rules.explanation: Delay mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy until stomatitis is grade 1 or less. This source does not specify a two-week stopping rule or a grade-specific stomatitis dose reduction. Assess bevacizumab independently.

action.recommendation: Review local PPE policy and discuss any dose modification with a Consultant.

rules.explanation: Clinically significant PPE requires local-policy and Consultant review.
No encoded FOLFOX hold, discontinuation, Consultant-review or component-modification rule was triggered.

action.recommendation: Withhold bevacizumab for uncontrolled or symptomatic hypertension on Day 1; initiate or adjust antihypertensive treatment.

rules.explanation: Withhold bevacizumab for uncontrolled or symptomatic hypertension on Day 1; initiate or adjust antihypertensive treatment.

action.recommendation: Discontinue the anti-VEGF component for severe haemorrhage.

rules.explanation: Discontinue the anti-VEGF component for severe haemorrhage.

action.recommendation: Discontinue bevacizumab for GI perforation, tracheoesophageal fistula or any grade 4 fistula.

rules.explanation: Discontinue bevacizumab for GI perforation, tracheoesophageal fistula or any grade 4 fistula.

action.recommendation: Discontinue the anti-VEGF component for an arterial thromboembolic event.

rules.explanation: Discontinue the anti-VEGF component for an arterial thromboembolic event.

action.recommendation: Withhold and obtain consultant review around surgery or impaired wound healing.

rules.explanation: Withhold and obtain consultant review around surgery or impaired wound healing.

action.recommendation: The source table does not assign bilirubin exactly 85 µmol/L or AST exactly 180 U/L. Obtain a Consultant dosing decision; do not infer a standard dose.

rules.explanation: The source table does not assign bilirubin exactly 85 µmol/L or AST exactly 180 U/L. Obtain a Consultant dosing decision; do not infer a standard dose.

action.recommendation: Hold bevacizumab; repeat 24-hour urine protein every two weeks. Resume on this criterion when protein is ≤2 g/24 h.

rules.explanation: Hold bevacizumab; repeat 24-hour urine protein every two weeks. Resume on this criterion when protein is ≤2 g/24 h.

action.recommendation: Discontinue bevacizumab when 24-hour urine protein exceeds 4 g/24 h.

rules.explanation: Discontinue bevacizumab when 24-hour urine protein exceeds 4 g/24 h.

action.recommendation: The 24-hour urine protein criterion permits bevacizumab at ≤2 g/24 h. Other bevacizumab criteria and unassessed domains still require review.

rules.explanation: The 24-hour urine protein criterion permits bevacizumab at ≤2 g/24 h. Other bevacizumab criteria and unassessed domains still require review.

action.recommendation: Withhold bevacizumab for a 4+ dipstick and collect 24-hour urine protein.

rules.explanation: Withhold bevacizumab for a 4+ dipstick and collect 24-hour urine protein.

action.recommendation: A 2+ or 3+ dipstick permits the scheduled bevacizumab dose on this criterion; collect 24-hour urine protein within three days before the next dose and apply the quantitative pathway. Any concurrent hold or stop criterion takes precedence.

rules.explanation: A 2+ or 3+ dipstick permits the scheduled bevacizumab dose on this criterion; collect 24-hour urine protein within three days before the next dose and apply the quantitative pathway. Any concurrent hold or stop criterion takes precedence.

action.recommendation: Discontinue bevacizumab for grade 4 proteinuria.

rules.explanation: Discontinue bevacizumab for grade 4 proteinuria.

action.recommendation: Consider a fluorouracil dose reduction in severe renal impairment only. The source does not quantify the reduction; obtain an individualised Consultant/pharmacy decision.

rules.explanation: Consider a fluorouracil dose reduction in severe renal impairment only. The source does not quantify the reduction; obtain an individualised Consultant/pharmacy decision.

action.recommendation: No renal-impairment studies are provided for bevacizumab in this source. Review suitability; do not infer a quantified dose reduction.

rules.explanation: No renal-impairment studies are provided for bevacizumab in this source. Review suitability; do not infer a quantified dose reduction.

action.recommendation: Oxaliplatin is contraindicated at CrCl <30 mL/min in NCCP 00446 Table 3. Do not substitute the 50% rule from a different FOLFOX regimen.

rules.explanation: Oxaliplatin is contraindicated at CrCl <30 mL/min in NCCP 00446 Table 3. Do not substitute the 50% rule from a different FOLFOX regimen.

action.recommendation: Exactly 30 mL/min is unassigned between the source table’s <30 and >30 rows. Obtain a Consultant decision; do not infer a normal or reduced dose.

rules.explanation: Exactly 30 mL/min is unassigned between the source table’s <30 and >30 rows. Obtain a Consultant decision; do not infer a normal or reduced dose.

action.recommendation: NCCP 00446 does not specify a dialysis dose or timing. Obtain a specialist plan; apply the CrCl contraindication if a verified CrCl <30 is supplied.

rules.explanation: NCCP 00446 does not specify a dialysis dose or timing. Obtain a specialist plan; apply the CrCl contraindication if a verified CrCl <30 is supplied.

action.recommendation: Fluorouracil is contraindicated when bilirubin exceeds 85 µmol/L or AST exceeds 180 U/L.

rules.explanation: Fluorouracil is contraindicated when bilirubin exceeds 85 µmol/L or AST exceeds 180 U/L.

action.recommendation: Moderate hepatic impairment: reduce the initial fluorouracil dose by one third; increase if no toxicity. Any bilirubin/AST contraindication takes precedence.

rules.explanation: Moderate hepatic impairment: reduce the initial fluorouracil dose by one third; increase if no toxicity. Any bilirubin/AST contraindication takes precedence.

action.recommendation: Severe hepatic impairment: reduce the initial fluorouracil dose by one half; increase if no toxicity. Any bilirubin/AST contraindication takes precedence.

rules.explanation: Severe hepatic impairment: reduce the initial fluorouracil dose by one half; increase if no toxicity. Any bilirubin/AST contraindication takes precedence.

action.recommendation: No hepatic-impairment studies are provided for bevacizumab in this source; review suitability without inventing a dose reduction.

rules.explanation: No hepatic-impairment studies are provided for bevacizumab in this source; review suitability without inventing a dose reduction.

action.recommendation: Hepatic-impairment information for oxaliplatin is limited. The source suggests a reduction is probably unnecessary; the dose remains a clinical decision.

rules.explanation: Hepatic-impairment information for oxaliplatin is limited. The source suggests a reduction is probably unnecessary; the dose remains a clinical decision.

crcl_ml_min.label: Creatinine clearance category

options.label: Dialysis — specialist review; no dose specified in this source

crcl_ml_min.assessment_guidance: Select the band containing verified creatinine clearance. Exactly 30 mL/min is not assigned in Table 3 and requires a Consultant decision. Dialysis has no separate quantified dose in this source.

neuropathy_grade.label: Peripheral neuropathy grade
neuropathy_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess sensory and/or motor symptoms and their effect on instrumental versus self-care activities of daily living. Distinguish transient cold sensitivity from persistent functional neuropathy.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No peripheral sensory or motor neuropathy.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only. CTCAE v5.0 grades symptomatic paraesthesia separately when that is the more accurate term.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate symptoms that limit instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms that limit self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening neurological consequences; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_current_grade.label: Current diarrhoea grade
diarrhoea_current_grade.assessment_guidance: Count stools per day above the patient's baseline, assess ostomy output, continence, hydration, fever, abdominal pain, haemodynamic compromise and whether hospital care is indicated.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Increase of 7 or more stools per day above baseline, incontinence, hospital care indicated, or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_highest_grade.label: Highest diarrhoea grade since previous cycle
diarrhoea_highest_grade.assessment_guidance: Count stools per day above the patient's baseline, assess ostomy output, continence, hydration, fever, abdominal pain, haemodynamic compromise and whether hospital care is indicated.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Increase of 7 or more stools per day above baseline, incontinence, hospital care indicated, or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

stomatitis_current_grade.label: Current stomatitis grade
stomatitis_current_grade.assessment_guidance: Inspect the oral cavity and assess pain, ulceration, diet modification and whether oral intake is impaired.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No oral mucositis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate pain or ulceration that does not interfere with oral intake; modified diet indicated.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe pain that interferes with oral intake.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

uncontrolled_hypertension.label: Uncontrolled or symptomatic hypertension on Day 1
uncontrolled_hypertension.assessment_guidance: NCCP defines uncontrolled hypertension for initiation as sustained BP >150/100 mmHg while receiving antihypertensive medication.

gi_perforation_or_fistula.label: GI perforation, tracheoesophageal fistula or any grade 4 fistula

recent_major_surgery_or_unhealed_wound.label: Recent major surgery or unhealed wound

renal_impairment_severity.label: Renal impairment severity
renal_impairment_severity.assessment_guidance: Use the clinically verified severity. NCCP does not provide a numeric cutoff or a percentage reduction for 5-FU in severe renal impairment in this regimen.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Oxaliplatin determines moderate emetic risk on the chemotherapy day; later infusion/tablet days follow the written individual plan.
